title: Anne Frank Remembered: The Story of the Woman Who Helped to Hide the Frank Family
author: Miep Gies with Alison Leslie Gold
target_audience: Educators and students studying World War II
Individuals seeking personal accounts of courage and resistance
Fans of Anne Frank’s diary wishing to know more about the people around her
General nonfiction readers interested in human resilience and ethics
core_themes: Courage and resistance in times of oppression
The moral imperative of helping others
Memory, testimony, and the responsibility of witnessing
The realities of hiding and survival
primary_purpose: To provide a firsthand account of Miep Gies, who risked her life to hide Anne Frank and her family during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands, offering insight into the events behind 'The Diary of Anne Frank' and honoring the quiet heroism of those who opposed tyranny.

structure_format.organization: Chronological memoir beginning with Miep's youth, covering the occupation, the hiding period, and the aftermath
features: Contextual information about the Frank family and supporting helpers
Descriptions of daily hardships and dangers
Reflections on the meaning of courage and humanity
Photo inserts and historical documentation (in some editions)

key_concepts_lessons: Acts of goodness can occur even in the darkest times.
Ordinary individuals are capable of extraordinary courage.
Resistance is not only armed—it can be quiet, personal, and persistent.
Bearing witness and telling the truth preserves memory and fosters understanding.
Fear and risk are ever-present, but compassion often outweighs personal safety.
History is made by the choices of everyday people.
notable_features: Firsthand account from a central figure in the Anne Frank story
Unique perspective on daily life in hiding during the Holocaust
Emphasizes untold stories of the helpers and the risks they faced
Contextualizes Anne Frank’s diary within broader events
Includes personal photographs and historical documentation in some editions
cultural_historical_context: Written decades after World War II, during a period of renewed public interest in Holocaust remembrance, survivor testimony, and ethical resistance, the memoir provided previously unseen details about the Frank family's final years and highlighted the bravery of ordinary citizens during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands.
reception_impact: Widely praised for its honesty, humility, and powerful storytelling
Considered an essential companion to 'The Diary of Anne Frank'
Frequently cited in educational settings for Holocaust studies
Recognized as a testament to quiet heroism and the importance of speaking out against repression
Inspires ongoing discussions about moral courage and responsibility
comparable_titles: The Diary of a Young Girl by Anne Frank
The Hiding Place by Corrie ten Boom
All But My Life by Gerda Weissmann Klein
Rena's Promise by Rena Kornreich Gelissen
They Dared Return by Patrick K. O'Donnell
